ak-fix.tagline: Fix bugs, errors, failing tests, and red CI after proving the cause.
ak-fix.summary: ak:fix takes a concrete symptom to a verified fix, requiring a proven root cause before any edit. It picks a quick, standard, or deep route by complexity, then reruns the original failing command and writes a journal entry.
howItWorks: Scouts affected files, then diagnoses with ak:debug; switches to ak:problem-solving after 2+ failed hypotheses.
Hard gate: needs symptom, repro, expected vs actual, file:line cause, and blast radius before editing.
Routes by size: 1 file → quick; 2-5 files → standard; 5+ files or architecture → deep with a plan.
Applies a minimal root-cause fix, reruns the failing command, adds a regression test, runs typecheck/lint/build/test.
Stops after 3 failed attempts; reviews the diff, runs /ak:journal, commits only with permission.
useWhen: A concrete error needs fixing: type error, failing test, logged exception, or red CI.
A UI bug needs a fix verified in a browser.
Several independent bugs can be fixed in parallel (--parallel).
avoidWhen: You only want the cause, not a fix: use ak:debug.
The work is a new feature: use ak:cook.
You want the full issue-to-PR pipeline: use ak:vibe.

params.name: [issue]
params.desc: Error, failing test, or CI link. If missing, the skill narrows it down from context.

params.name: --auto
params.desc: Default. Runs fix and verify within scope; asks only for key decisions or destructive actions.

params.name: --review
params.desc: Pauses for approval at each major step. Best for production, security, or system-wide bugs.

params.name: --quick
params.desc: Lean route: scout → diagnose → fix → verify → review. Escalates if architecture decisions appear. Conflicts with --ultra.

params.name: --parallel
params.desc: Fixes independent issues with separate file ownership in parallel. Conflicts with --ultra.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: Generates 5 read-only fix-plans after diagnosis; a verifier picks one or rejects all. Hard-stops with --quick or --parallel.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: Kongming advises after each step, when stuck, and before high-risk decisions. It writes no code.

params.name: --skip-journal
params.desc: Skips the automatic /ak:journal. Also skipped when journal.auto=false.

examples.cmd: /ak:fix "TS2345 in src/auth/session.ts after upgrading zod" --quick
examples.note: Single-file type error; the checker is the regression proof.

examples.cmd: /ak:fix login sometimes returns 401 even though the token is still valid
examples.note: Unclear multi-file cause: standard route, auto mode.

examples.cmd: /ak:fix memory leak in worker queue --ultra --advice

tips: Paste the exact error and repro command; the root-cause gate needs both.
--ultra and the deep route cost many tokens; save them for hard bugs.
The skill never commits or pushes; use ak:git or ak:ship afterward.

ak-debug.tagline: Investigate systematically and prove the root cause before any fix.
ak-debug.summary: ak:debug investigates code-level failures and system incidents (CI/CD, performance, databases, logs). It allows no fix without a proven root cause and no "done" without fresh verification evidence.
howItWorks: Classifies the problem: code bug, stack error, system incident, CI/CD, performance, or frontend.
Code bugs: root-cause investigation → pattern analysis → hypothesis testing → implementation.
Traces the call stack back to the trigger; scripts/find-polluter.sh bisects test pollution.
Collects logs via gh CLI, psql, and log queries; checks frontend issues in a browser.
--ultra runs 5 read-only diagnoses on one evidence packet; a verifier picks one or rejects all.
useWhen: A test fails or behavior is wrong and the cause is unknown.
CI fails, the system is slow, or a production incident spans components.
A test fails only in the full suite (test pollution).
avoidWhen: The cause is known and you need a fix: use ak:fix.
You have a diagnosis and need to compare solutions: use ak:brainstorm.
You only need to find related files: use ak:scout.

params.name: [error or issue description]
params.desc: Error, stack trace, or symptom to investigate.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: Best-of-5: 5 independent read-only diagnoses, a verifier picks one or rejects all. The winner still needs fresh verification.

examples.cmd: /ak:debug test UserService.spec.ts fails randomly when running the full suite
examples.note: Suspected test pollution: bisect with find-polluter.sh.

examples.cmd: /ak:debug workflow deploy.yml fails at the build step since commit abc1234
examples.note: Reads CI logs via gh CLI.

examples.cmd: /ak:debug race condition when 2 webhooks arrive at the same time --ultra
examples.note: Hard bug: 5 diagnoses plus a verifier.

tips: A minimal repro and real logs cut investigation rounds and tokens.
Treat "probably X" or "seems fixed" as red flags; demand evidence.
Debug does not fix; switch to /ak:fix once the cause is proven.

ak-test.tagline: Run, create, optimize, and audit test suites with QA reports.
ak-test.summary: ak:test runs code tests, browser UI tests, coverage, and build checks, then writes a QA report. Subcommands ui, create, optimize, and audit test sites, build suites, cut CI cost, or expose deceptive tests, and never skip or fake failing tests.
howItWorks: No argument shows a menu: default, ui, create, optimize, audit. With context, starts immediately.
Default: scopes from recent changes, runs narrow checks, then the suite, coverage, and a report.
ui tests a URL for screenshots, responsiveness, accessibility, forms, and console errors.
create and optimize apply changes directly; audit only reports ranked findings.
optimize and audit spawn parallel scouts; --ultra adds 5 candidates plus a verifier.
useWhen: You just changed code and need proof nothing broke before committing.
You want a website UI tested, including logged-in routes.
CI is slow (optimize) or the suite seems unreliable (audit).
avoidWhen: A test fails and you need the cause fixed: use ak:fix or ak:debug.
You need edge cases before coding: use ak:scenario.
You need load, visual regression, or cross-browser tests: use ak:web-testing.

params.name: [context]
params.desc: Test scope: file, module, or feature. Empty shows the operation menu.

params.name: ui [url]
params.desc: UI tests on the URL. Logged-in routes use ak:chrome-profile.

params.name: create [scope]
params.desc: Builds a coverage matrix, then designs and writes a suite. Applies directly unless --interview is set.

params.name: optimize [scope]
params.desc: Cuts test time and cost at equal safety. Applies directly unless --interview.

params.name: audit [scope]
params.desc: Reports ranked, evidence-backed findings with fix suggestions. Fixes only on separate request.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: With create/optimize/audit: kongming advises before suite/CI changes and when stuck. Never overrides failing-test rules.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: With create/optimize/audit: 5 read-only candidates + verifier; audit merges verified findings.

params.name: --interview
params.desc: With create/optimize/audit: lists each proposed change with a reason and applies only approved groups.

examples.cmd: /ak:test src/payments
examples.note: Tests the changed module and reports.

examples.cmd: /ak:test ui https://staging.example.com
examples.note: Staging UI: screenshots, responsive, a11y, console errors.

examples.cmd: /ak:test create packages/api --interview
examples.note: New API suite, approving each test group.

tips: create and optimize apply changes by default; add --interview to approve CI workflow edits.
audit only reports; ask explicitly for fixes.
For logged-in tests use ak:chrome-profile, never paste cookies into chat.
artifacts: QA report: results, coverage, failures, build status
New or updated test files (create, optimize)

ak-code-review.tagline: Evidence-based review of pending changes, PRs, commits, or a codebase.
ak-code-review.summary: ak:code-review checks the target against spec, regressions, security, and repo conventions, with file/line evidence for every finding. It detects the input type itself, and review-only mode never edits, posts, or merges.
howItWorks: Detects input: PR number/URL → gh diff; commit hash → git show; --pending → git diff HEAD.
Runs an edge-case scout, then Stage 1 spec compliance (if a plan exists) and Stage 2 code quality.
codebase runs parallel researchers and reviewers; a planner writes an improvement plan.
codebase parallel splits edge cases into at most 6 groups, one reviewer each.
--ultra fans Stage 2 to 5 read-only reviewers; a verifier returns the deduplicated union.
useWhen: You want local changes reviewed before committing (--pending).
You need a PR or suspect commit reviewed.
You need a whole-codebase audit for bugs, security risks, and tech debt.
avoidWhen: You want to post comments, fix, and merge a PR: use ak:review-pr.
You only need security or secret scanning: use ak:security.
You want a finished branch shipped: use ak:ship.

params.name: #PR
params.desc: PR number (#123) or GitHub PR URL; fetches the diff via gh.

params.name: COMMIT
params.desc: 7-40 character commit hash; reviews it via git show. Must exist locally.

params.name: --pending
params.desc: Reviews staged + unstaged changes vs HEAD; asks for a short intent.

params.name: codebase
params.desc: Full scan with parallel researchers and reviewers; a planner builds an improvement plan, then offers commit/push.

params.name: codebase parallel
params.desc: Lists edge cases, splits them into at most 6 groups, one reviewer per group. Conflicts with --ultra.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: 5 independent read-only Stage 2 reviewers; verifier merges verified findings. Hard-stops with codebase parallel.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: Kongming advises after each stage, when stuck, and before high-risk verdicts.

params.name: --yagni
params.desc: Adds recommendations to cut scope not needed for the outcome; reviewers keep full scope by default.

examples.cmd: /ak:code-review --pending
/ak:code-review 3f9a2c1
examples.note: Check a commit suspected of a regression.

examples.cmd: /ak:code-review codebase parallel
examples.note: Audit the codebase with reviewers split by edge-case group.

tips: Review-only never edits or posts; use ak:review-pr to post to GitHub.
codebase modes spawn many subagents; a typo does not need them.
Findings that contradict current source or tests get rejected with evidence.

ak-ship.tagline: One command: test, review, version, changelog, commit, push, open PR.
ak-ship.summary: ak:ship runs a 14-step pipeline that takes a feature branch to a PR, with optional review-merge and a build-in-public post. It detects official (main/master) or beta (dev/beta/develop) mode and returns the PR URL with a per-step status table.
howItWorks: Picks mode from the token or branch name; asks when unclear. Stops if already on target.
Merges origin/<target>, runs tests (tester) and a 2-pass review (code-reviewer).
Bumps version and changelog if present; asks only for major/minor bumps.
Commits, pushes without force, opens a PR with a 7-section evidence body; docs update only in official.
--merge runs ak:review-pr to fix, merge, and wait for green CI; --social drafts a post.
useWhen: A feature branch is done and you want tests, review, and a PR in one command.
You want the PR auto-reviewed, merged, and CI-verified (--merge).
You ship beta first, then promote to stable (--both).
avoidWhen: You only need a plain commit/push: use ak:git.
Tests are red from an unfixed bug: use ak:fix first.
You want to deploy an app to hosting: use ak:deploy.

params.name: official | stable | main
params.desc: Ships to main/master with the full pipeline, including docs and journal.

params.name: beta | dev | next
params.desc: Ships to dev/beta/develop, skipping docs. Without a token: base main/master → official, else beta.

params.name: --both
params.desc: Ships beta, then a gated stable stage. Overrides the mode token. --dry-run simulates only beta.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: Kongming supervises at key checkpoints; passed to ak:review-pr with --merge.

params.name: --merge
params.desc: Runs ak:review-pr <PR> --fix --reply --merge. Claims success only when approved, merged, and CI is green.

params.name: --skip-tests
params.desc: Skips tests; use only with passing-test evidence on the same revision.

params.name: --skip-review
params.desc: Skips the pre-landing review; the --merge review still runs.

params.name: --skip-journal
params.desc: Skips the journal step; also skips the whole --social step.

params.name: --skip-docs
params.desc: Skips the docs update.

params.name: --social
params.desc: Drafts a build-in-public post after the PR. Refuses on red CI.

params.name: --yes-post
params.desc: Required with --social to actually post; otherwise drafts only.

params.name: --yes-post-private
params.desc: Required with --social --yes-post on private repos as a second confirmation.

params.name: --dry-run
params.desc: Shows the plan without executing; stops before kongming, ak:review-pr, and posting.

examples.cmd: /ak:ship
examples.note: Detects mode from the branch, runs the full pipeline.

examples.cmd: /ak:ship official --advice --merge
examples.note: Ship to main under kongming, then merge on green CI.

examples.cmd: /ak:ship --dry-run
examples.note: Preview the pipeline before your first ship.

tips: Nothing publishes on red tests; --skip-tests needs same-revision proof.
Only this task's files get committed; unrelated dirty files stay untouched.
--social is dry-run by default; posting needs --yes-post.
artifacts: Pushed commit and PR with evidence body

ak-loop.tagline: Optimization loop: change, measure a metric, keep or revert via git.
ak-loop.summary: ak:loop improves a shell-measurable metric (coverage, bundle size, lint errors) by repeating modify → verify → keep or discard, committing each atomic change first. You give a config block (Goal, Scope, Verify) and need a git repo with a clean tree.
howItWorks: Asks once for missing Goal, Scope, or Verify; rejects dangerous Verify commands.
Records a baseline; Guard must pass at baseline.
Each iteration edits only Scope with one atomic change and commits before measuring.
Keeps or reverts by Noise, Min-Delta, and Direction; failed Guard or timeout means discard.
Logs each iteration to loop-results.tsv; 5 discards changes strategy, 10 stops.
useWhen: You want coverage raised to a threshold or bundle size under a target.
You want lint or type errors driven to zero in small steps.
You have a shell-measurable metric and want automated experiments with rollback.
avoidWhen: The goal is subjective or one-off: use ak:cook.
The bug has a known cause: use ak:fix.
No mechanical metric exists: use ak:cook --interactive.

params.name: [Goal/Metric description]
params.desc: Goal or metric in words, or the full config block below the command.

params.name: Goal
params.desc: Required. Human-readable target, like 'Increase test coverage in src/utils'.

params.name: Scope
params.desc: Required. Glob of files the loop may edit. Nothing outside Scope changes.

params.name: Verify
params.desc: Required. Shell command printing exactly one number; runs every iteration after a safety screen.

params.name: Guard
params.desc: Optional. Regression check (exit 0 = pass); its files are read-only.

params.name: Iterations
params.desc: Optional, default 10. Maximum iterations.

params.name: Noise
params.desc: Optional, default medium. Variance tolerance: low / medium / high.

params.name: Min-Delta
params.desc: Optional, default 0. Minimum improvement that counts.

params.name: Direction
params.desc: Optional, default higher. Whether higher or lower is better.

params.name: Timeout
params.desc: Optional, default 30s. Per-verify deadline; overruns are discarded.

examples.cmd:
/ak:loop
Goal: Reduce main bundle size below 200KB
Scope: src/**/*.ts, src/**/*.tsx
Verify: npx vite build 2>/dev/null | grep "dist/index" | awk '{print $2}' | sed 's/kB//'
Guard: npx tsc --noEmit
Direction: lower
Min-Delta: 0.5
examples.note: Shrink bundle, ignoring swings under 0.5 kB.

examples.cmd: /ak:loop improve the Lighthouse performance score of the /pricing page
examples.note: Goal only; the skill asks for missing fields.

tips: Always set a Guard; coverage gained by weakening tests is a regression.
Cost scales with Iterations; time one Verify run first.
For noisy metrics, set Noise high or Min-Delta above 0.
artifacts: One git commit per iteration (kept or reverted)

ak-bootstrap.tagline: Start a new project from idea to running, tested code.
ak-bootstrap.summary: ak:bootstrap takes a new-project idea through research, stack choice, design, plan, implementation, tests, review, and docs. It writes no code itself, delegating to ak:plan and ak:cook with flags per mode.
howItWorks: Opens with a brainstorm gate; reuses existing code without resetting and inits git only for new projects.
Full mode: clarifies, runs parallel researchers, writes 2-3 stack options to ./docs.
Offers design: HTML wireframes in ./docs/wireframe/ and a logo; --fast skips this gate.
Plans via /ak:plan, then builds via /ak:cook with the mode's flag.
Tester, debugger, code-reviewer, and docs-manager finish; commits only on request.
useWhen: You are starting a brand-new project from an idea.
You want a quick prototype and accept skipping design (--fast).
The project is large and suits parallel agents (--parallel).
avoidWhen: You are adding a feature to an existing project: use ak:plan + ak:cook.
You only need a plan: use ak:plan.
You only want to explore the idea: use ak:brainstorm.

params.name: [requirements]
params.desc: Project description: product, key features, constraints.

params.name: --full
params.desc: Default. Full workflow; asks key decisions; plans with /ak:plan --hard.

params.name: --auto
params.desc: Autonomous: no research/stack gates, picks the best option; plan and cook run --auto.

params.name: --fast
params.desc: Batched research, no design gate; plan --fast. The opening brainstorm gate still applies.

params.name: --parallel
params.desc: Multi-agent: plan and cook run --parallel with file ownership. Conflicts with --ultra.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: Plans with /ak:plan --ultra (best-of-5); cook keeps the mode flag. Hard-stops with --parallel.

params.name: --yagni
params.desc: Cuts scope not needed for the outcome; passed to ak:plan and ak:cook.

params.name: --skip-journal
params.desc: Skips the final /ak:journal; also skipped when journal.auto=false.

examples.cmd: /ak:bootstrap "Build a SaaS dashboard with auth"
examples.note: Full workflow with research, stack, and design.

examples.cmd: /ak:bootstrap "Build a SaaS dashboard with auth" --fast
/ak:bootstrap "E-commerce platform with Stripe" --parallel

tips: Token cost is high; use --fast for prototypes.
State your preferred stack up front to skip stack selection.
Bootstrap never pushes; use ak:git or ak:ship.

ak-agentize.tagline: Turn existing code or APIs into an agent-friendly CLI or MCP server.
ak-agentize.summary: ak:agentize wraps an existing codebase or module as a CLI with structured output, an MCP server, or both. It maps exports, side effects, and credentials, decides the surface, then scaffolds, wraps, hardens, and packages.
howItWorks: Scouts exports, schemas, callers, side effects, and credentials; builds an Agentization Map.
Decides CLI/MCP/both, local or remote, and auth; --ask interviews you first.
Keeps business logic separate from adapters; CLI gets deterministic output and exit codes.
MCP keeps stdio logs off stdout and uses OAuth for remote servers.
Verifies original behavior through each adapter; packages but publishes only on request.
useWhen: An internal library should be callable by agents over MCP.
You want a JSON-output CLI for headless agent runs.
A large REST/OpenAPI API needs curated agent workflows.
avoidWhen: You are building an MCP server from scratch: use ak:mcp-builder.
You want in-browser agent tools: use ak:webmcp.
You are writing a SKILL.md: use ak:skill-creator.

params.name: [feature-or-module]
params.desc: Module or feature to agentize; empty means the whole codebase.

params.name: --both
params.desc: Default. CLI and MCP adapters on shared logic; hardening checks both.

params.name: --mcp
params.desc: MCP server only. Also inferred from 'MCP only'.

params.name: --cli
params.desc: CLI only. Inferred from 'CLI only' or 'npm package'.

params.name: --auto
params.desc: Default. Analyzes, decides, and implements without asking.

params.name: --ask
params.desc: Asks clarifying and challenge questions after analysis. With --ultra, the interview runs once before fan-out.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: Fans the map and decision to 5 read-only candidates; a verifier picks one or rejects all.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: Kongming advises after analysis, before locking decisions, before packaging, and when stuck.

params.name: --yagni
params.desc: Cuts scope not needed for the outcome; passed to subagents.

examples.cmd: /ak:agentize src/billing
examples.note: Default: CLI and MCP for the billing module.

examples.cmd: /ak:agentize packages/search --mcp --ask
examples.note: MCP only; clarify transport and auth first.

examples.cmd: /ak:agentize --cli --yagni
examples.note: Minimal CLI for the whole codebase.

tips: If nothing is exposable, the skill names the needed refactor.
MCP stdio logs on stdout break the protocol.
Packaging is not publishing; request npm or Cloudflare releases explicitly.

ak-backend-development.tagline: Build backends and APIs in Node.js, Python, or Go.
ak-backend-development.summary: ak:backend-development builds REST/GraphQL/gRPC APIs, auth, security, performance, and microservices in the project's real stack. It verifies both success and failure paths and hands database, auth, or deploy work to specialized skills.
howItWorks: Reads manifests, service boundaries, and tests to find the real stack; never swaps it unasked.
Classifies the change and loads only the matching reference (API, auth, OWASP, performance, architecture).
States trade-offs for new choices; checks version-sensitive advice against installed deps.
Validates input, keeps authorization server-side, returns stable errors.
Verifies success and failure paths plus affected callers.
useWhen: You need a new endpoint in NestJS, FastAPI, Django, Express, or Go.
You need OWASP fixes or backend performance work.
You are designing microservices, events, CQRS, or sagas.
avoidWhen: Schema, query, or migration work: use ak:databases.
Better Auth integration: use ak:better-auth.
Deploy or infrastructure: use ak:deploy or ak:devops.

params.name: [framework]
params.desc: Target framework or language, like nestjs, fastapi, django, go. The stack in manifests still wins.

params.name: [task]
params.desc: Backend task: API, auth, performance, architecture, testing, deployment.

examples.cmd: /ak:backend-development nestjs add cursor pagination endpoint for /orders
examples.note: Pagination in an existing NestJS service.

examples.cmd: /ak:backend-development fastapi OWASP audit for the upload module
/ak:backend-development go add Redis cache for product lookup

tips: Recipe performance numbers are not evidence; measure your baseline.
Name the change type so only the needed reference loads.
Ask for failure-path tests, not just the happy path.
artifacts: Backend source (routes, services, middleware) and tests

ak-better-auth.tagline: Add Better Auth to TypeScript apps: OAuth, 2FA, passkeys, sessions.
ak-better-auth.summary: ak:better-auth integrates Better Auth into TypeScript apps on Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Remix, Astro, Hono, and Express. It checks the installed version and schema first and scaffolds only for new integrations.
howItWorks: Checks the installed version, server/client wiring, and existing schema.
New setups pick an auth method and may run scripts/better_auth_init.py.
Existing setups never rerun init; plugins (twoFactor, passkey, magicLink, organization) come from references.
Checks security advisories and keeps key invariants like single-use magic links.
Verifies callback failure and session expiry/revocation; keeps secrets server-side.
useWhen: You want email/password or Google/GitHub OAuth in a TypeScript app.
You want 2FA, passkeys, or magic links on a Better Auth app.
You need organizations with member invites.
avoidWhen: The project uses Auth.js, Clerk, or Supabase Auth: use ak:backend-development.
ASP.NET Core auth: use dotnet-claude-kit:authentication.
Full security audit: use ak:security.

params.name: [auth-method or feature]
params.desc: Auth method or feature to add, like oauth github, 2fa, passkey, organization, rate limiting.

examples.cmd: /ak:better-auth email/password + email verification for a Next.js app
/ak:better-auth enable the twoFactor plugin
/ak:better-auth organization with email invitations

tips: Never rerun init to add plugins; it can overwrite config.
Run schema migrations after adding plugins that need tables.
Check advisories for your exact version before calling a vulnerability patched.
artifacts: Route handlers and sign-in UI (when needed)

ak-databases.tagline: Design schemas, queries, indexes, and migrations for MongoDB and PostgreSQL.
ak-databases.summary: ak:databases covers MongoDB and PostgreSQL schema design, queries, indexes, migrations, replication, and backups. It detects the engine and version, and demands evidence by impact: EXPLAIN for performance, rollback for migrations, approval for destructive actions.
howItWorks: Detects engine and version; keeps the engine unless asked to change.
Performance changes need EXPLAIN plus before/after numbers; ANALYZE really executes the query.
Migrations need a backup, rollback, and safe reruns.
Backup, restore, and admin need an exact target and explicit approval.
Uses db_migrate.py, db_backup.py, and db_performance_check.py when they fit.
useWhen: You are designing an app or analytics schema.
A query is slow and needs EXPLAIN and index suggestions.
You need a safe migration or backup/replication setup.
avoidWhen: You only need read-only data for debugging: use dbread.
EF Core in .NET: use dotnet-claude-kit:ef-core.
API logic not centered on the database: use ak:backend-development.

params.name: [query or schema task]
params.desc: Database task: query, schema, index, migration, backup, optimization.

examples.cmd: /ak:databases design a PostgreSQL schema for a multi-branch booking system
/ak:databases MongoDB aggregation of revenue by month and category
/ak:databases migration adding a NOT NULL tenant_id column to users

tips: EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs the query; take care with writes on production.
Give the engine version and table structure so the skill does not guess.
Performance claims need workload numbers, not just a plan.

ak-deploy.tagline: Deploy to 15 platforms with auto-detection, health checks, and rollback.
ak-deploy.summary: ak:deploy resolves the environment and target from config and docs, then deploys to platforms like Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare, Fly.io, Render, and AWS. A deploy counts only with health evidence and a recorded rollback; infra, migrations, DNS, and SSL are out of scope.
howItWorks: Resolves environment and target first; flags doc/config conflicts to avoid hitting production by mistake.
Detects the platform from files like vercel.json, netlify.toml, wrangler.toml, fly.toml.
With no target, classifies the project and offers up to 4 platforms.
Checks CLI and auth, then runs only commands from references/platforms/<platform>.md.
Verifies URL, health, revision, and environment; records the rollback command.
useWhen: You want to deploy or host the current app.
You do not know where to host and need options compared.
You need health and rollback verified on a configured platform.
avoidWhen: Kubernetes, CI/CD, or infra provisioning: use ak:devops.
"Ship" meaning branch to PR: use ak:ship.
You only ask about a provider without deploy intent.

params.name: [platform]
params.desc: One of 15 platforms: vercel, netlify, cloudflare, railway, flyio, render, heroku, tose, github-pages, coolify, dokploy, gcp, aws, digitalocean, vultr. Empty auto-detects.

params.name: [environment]
params.desc: Target environment: preview, staging, or production. Resolved first to avoid accidental production deploys.

examples.cmd: /ak:deploy
/ak:deploy vercel preview
examples.note: Vercel preview with a verified URL.

examples.cmd: /ak:deploy flyio production
examples.note: Production deploy with health check and rollback.

tips: Naming a provider is not deploy intent; say clearly when to deploy.
With conflicting configs, name platform and environment explicitly.
Keep the recorded rollback command after each production deploy.
artifacts: Rollback note or previous deploy ID

ak-devops.tagline: Cloudflare, Docker, GCP, Kubernetes, CI/CD, GitOps, and infra audits.
ak-devops.summary: ak:devops builds and manages infrastructure on Cloudflare, Docker, Google Cloud, and Kubernetes, plus CI/CD, GitOps, and security audits. It keeps the repo's provider and requires exact account, region, health check, and rollback for production.
howItWorks: Reads the repo's deploy and container config; keeps that provider.
Picks an explicit effect: local, preview, or production; local Docker never calls cloud CLIs.
Loads only the target's references; uses cloudflare_deploy.py and docker_optimize.py when they fit.
Production pins account/project/region, a health check, and rollback.
Updates ops docs via /ak:docs when deploy, log, or credential paths change.
useWhen: You deploy Cloudflare Workers with R2, D1, or KV.
You need a Dockerfile, Compose setup, or Cloud Run/GKE deploy.
You manage Kubernetes, GitOps, CI/CD, or an infra security audit.
avoidWhen: A simple app deploy to a PaaS: use ak:deploy.
.NET containers or CI/CD: use dotnet-claude-kit:container-publish or ci-cd.
Source code secret scanning: use ak:security.

/ak:devops docker write a non-root multi-stage Dockerfile for a Node app
/ak:devops gcp deploy to Cloud Run in region asia-southeast1
examples.note: Production with health check and rollback.

tips: Name account, project, and region for production.
Kubernetes/Helm have no dedicated reference; state your versions.
Check for orphaned dev processes like wrangler dev or docker compose up.

ak-mobile-development.tagline: Build mobile apps with React Native, Flutter, SwiftUI, or Compose.
ak-mobile-development.summary: ak:mobile-development builds iOS/Android apps covering UX, performance, offline-first, security, testing, and store releases. It keeps the existing framework for small changes and requires real-device measurements for performance claims.
howItWorks: Reads manifests and platform files to find framework, toolchain, and devices.
Keeps existing architecture; compares frameworks only when the platform choice is open.
Loads iOS, Android, best-practice, or debugging references as needed.
Sets performance budgets from target devices and baseline; records untested devices.
Checks current Apple/Google submission rules before release.
useWhen: You are building a feature in a React Native, Flutter, SwiftUI, or Compose app.
The app janks, drains battery, or uses too much memory.
You are preparing an App Store or Google Play release.
avoidWhen: A responsive web app: use ak:frontend-development or ak:web-frameworks.
UI/UX design only: use ak:ui-ux-pro-max.
The app's backend API: use ak:backend-development.

params.name: [platform]
params.desc: Platform or framework: ios, android, react-native, flutter, swiftui, compose.

params.name: [feature]
params.desc: Feature or task: screen, offline sync, push notifications, performance tuning, release.

examples.cmd: /ak:mobile-development react-native add a list screen with infinite scroll
examples.note: UI feature in an existing app.

examples.cmd: /ak:mobile-development ios app crashes when opening the camera
/ak:mobile-development choose React Native or Flutter for a booking app

Name the framework when the repo has several mobile projects.
Keep secure storage and accessibility intact even for small edits.

ak-tanstack.tagline: Build with TanStack Start, Form, and AI, matched to installed versions.
ak-tanstack.summary: ak:tanstack covers TanStack Start/Router routes, server functions, middleware, TanStack Form validation, and TanStack AI streaming chat, using the installed package versions. TanStack Query, Table, and Virtual are out of scope.
howItWorks: Reads manifests, lockfile, and imports to find installed TanStack versions.
Loads only the Start, Form, or AI reference the task needs.
Never hand-edits routeTree.gen.ts; edits routes and runs the generator.
Verifies types, build, and affected behavior with existing scripts.
useWhen: You are building a TanStack Start app with file routes and server functions.
You need a validated form in TanStack Form.
You want streaming AI chat in a TanStack app.
avoidWhen: TanStack Query, Table, Virtual: use ak:frontend-development.
Next.js App Router apps: use ak:web-frameworks.
Generic React patterns: use ak:react-best-practices.

params.desc: TanStack part: start, router, form, ai.

params.desc: Feature: route, server function, middleware, form validation, AI chat.

/ak:tanstack ai streaming chat with tool calling

TanStack APIs change fast; installed types win over examples.

ak-web-frameworks.tagline: Next.js App Router and Turborepo monorepos, with optional RemixIcon.
ak-web-frameworks.summary: ak:web-frameworks builds Next.js apps (routing, Server Components, data fetching, caching) and Turborepo monorepos (workspaces, pipelines, remote cache). Scripts initialize Next.js projects and migrate monorepos to Turborepo.
howItWorks: Reads manifests and config; keeps the chosen framework and icon library.
Loads Next.js or Turborepo references matching the change.
Uses nextjs_init.py for new apps and turborepo_migrate.py (supports --dry-run) for monorepos.
Defaults to Server Components, loading/error states, and an explicit caching strategy.
Uses the patched stable Next.js line, never canary.
useWhen: You are building a Next.js App Router app with RSC, SSR, or ISR.
You are setting up a Turborepo monorepo.
Monorepo builds are slow and need pipelines and remote cache.
avoidWhen: Deep React render performance: use ak:react-best-practices.
TanStack Start: use ak:tanstack.
Deploying to Vercel/Netlify: use ak:deploy.

/ak:web-frameworks turborepo migrate the existing pnpm monorepo to Turborepo

Declare outputs in turbo.json or caching will not work.
Use ^build for topological dependencies between packages.

ak-payment-integration.tagline: Integrate SePay (VietQR), Polar, and Stripe payments safely.
ak-payment-integration.summary: ak:payment-integration implements checkout, webhooks, and subscriptions with SePay for Vietnam, Polar for global SaaS, and Stripe for enterprise. It verifies webhook signatures on the raw payload, dedupes events, and lets only the server own amount and status.
howItWorks: Keeps the current provider and API version unless asked to change.
New setups: SePay for VietQR, Polar for SaaS subscriptions, Stripe for enterprise/Connect.
Builds auth → products → checkout → webhooks → events, loading only needed recipes.
Verifies signatures on the raw body and dedupes with idempotency keys.
Tests duplicate and out-of-order events in sandbox; a client redirect never proves payment.
useWhen: You want VietQR bank-transfer payments via SePay.
You sell SaaS subscriptions via Polar or Stripe.
You need idempotent webhooks or multi-provider orders.
avoidWhen: Billing inside a Shopify app: use ak:shopify.
Backend APIs unrelated to payments: use ak:backend-development.

params.name: [provider]
params.desc: Provider: sepay, polar, stripe, or multi-provider.

params.name: [task]
params.desc: Task: checkout, webhook, subscription, QR code, benefits, API version upgrade, order management.

examples.cmd: /ak:payment-integration sepay create a VietQR for an order and confirm via webhook
/ak:payment-integration polar monthly/yearly subscription with trial
/ak:payment-integration stripe idempotent webhook for checkout.session.completed

tips: Fulfill only on signature-verified webhooks, never on client redirects.
Parsing JSON before verifying breaks the signature.
Test in sandbox; use the stripe CLI to forward webhooks locally.

ak-shopify.tagline: Build Shopify apps, extensions, and themes with Shopify CLI.
ak-shopify.summary: ak:shopify detects whether the work is an app, extension, or theme and reads the configured CLI and API versions first. It keeps OAuth scopes minimal, verifies webhooks, and tests on a development store or preview theme.
howItWorks: Resolves app, extension, or theme; never scaffolds an app just to edit a theme.
Reads configured Shopify CLI and API versions before running commands.
Loads app, extension, or theme references; scripts/shopify_init.py sets up new projects.
Keeps scopes minimal, verifies webhook signatures, holds billing state server-side.
Verifies on a dev store or preview theme; cleans up tunnels it started.
useWhen: You are building an embedded app with OAuth, webhooks, and billing.
You need a checkout, admin, or POS extension, or Shopify Functions.
You are customizing a Liquid theme or debugging webhooks and rate limits.
avoidWhen: Payments outside Shopify: use ak:payment-integration.
Headless Next.js storefronts: use ak:web-frameworks.
Store marketing strategy: use the marketing skills.

Prefer GraphQL and request only needed fields.
On rate limits, use backoff or bulk operations.

ak-mcp-builder.tagline: Build MCP servers in Python or TypeScript, one complete tool first.
ak-mcp-builder.summary: ak:mcp-builder builds MCP servers that connect LLMs to external services, starting with one complete, validated tool. It then runs the server against a real client and writes task-based evaluations.
howItWorks: Defines the task and first tool contract; checks the project's SDK and transport.
Implements one tool with accurate annotations, input limits, actionable errors, and timeouts.
Enforces auth and scopes in code; annotations are only hints.
Runs the server with a real client and confirms output and effects.
Writes 10 read-only evaluation questions and runs scripts/evaluation.py.
useWhen: You need an MCP server for an external API.
You are designing tool schemas, pagination, and errors.
You want an evaluation suite for an MCP server.
avoidWhen: Wrapping existing repo code: use ak:agentize.
In-browser agent tools: use ak:webmcp.
Just calling existing MCP tools: use the runtime's native tools.

params.desc: Service or API to integrate through an MCP server.

/ak:mcp-builder Node SDK for Jira, streamable HTTP transport
/ak:mcp-builder write a 10-question evaluation for an existing Slack MCP server

tips: Get one tool working end to end before adding more.
Registration is not proof; run it with a real client.
Evaluation answers must be stable and need only read-only operations.

ak-google-adk-python.tagline: Build Google ADK Python agents: multi-agent, A2A, MCP tools, Vertex deploys.
ak-google-adk-python.summary: ak:google-adk-python builds, evaluates, and deploys agents with Google's Agent Development Kit, including multi-agent systems, A2A, MCP tools, workflow agents, and memory. An agent folder needs __init__.py and an agent.py defining root_agent or app.
howItWorks: Checks installed ADK version; keeps the root_agent/app entrypoint.
Loads the reference for the intent: agents, multi-agent/A2A, tools/MCP, state, callbacks, deployment.
Checks examples against the installed SDK and current model catalog.
Verifies tool side effects and error paths; evaluates with adk eval.
Starts minimal and expands only for the requested workflow.
useWhen: You are building a Gemini agent with tools in ADK Python.
You need sub-agents, A2A, or MCP servers as tools.
You deploy to Cloud Run, Vertex AI Agent Engine, or GKE.
avoidWhen: Claude API or Agent SDK agents: use claude-api.
Building an MCP server: use ak:mcp-builder.
GCP infrastructure unrelated to ADK: use ak:devops.

params.desc: ADK agent or feature: single agent, multi-agent, A2A, MCP tool, workflow, memory, callback, deploy, eval.

Start with one minimal agent before adding sub-agents.

ak-webmcp.tagline: Expose website features as WebMCP tools for in-browser agents.
ak-webmcp.summary: ak:webmcp turns website features into WebMCP tools that in-browser agents call via document.modelContext instead of scraping the DOM. WebMCP is a W3C draft browser API, not an Anthropic MCP server.
howItWorks: Feature-detects the API; keeps the normal UI when unsupported.
Plans a small set of non-overlapping tools with exact names and specific schemas.
Simple forms use the declarative API; stateful actions use imperative registerTool.
Adds safety hints (readOnly, consequential, untrustedContent) and limits cross-origin exposure.
Scaffolds with scaffold_tool.py, validates with validate_webmcp.mjs, then runs evals.
useWhen: You want agent tools on an existing website.
You want forms or page actions callable by in-browser agents.
You are integrating WebMCP into React or Angular.
avoidWhen: Building stdio/HTTP MCP servers: use ak:mcp-builder.
Browser automation or testing: use ak:agent-browser.
Wrapping backend code as CLI/MCP: use ak:agentize.

tips: Treat tool output and page text as untrusted data, not instructions.
Enforce authorization inside execute, not only via schema.
Keep the tool set small; every tool costs agent context.
